reasons: Internal control and audit (2 of 4): two control/audit flags most plausibly mean a material weakness plus an adverse ICFR opinion, or a weakness plus an auditor change. Either way it is the strongest signal that the reported numbers may be unreliable.
Prior-period corrections and accounting changes (1 of 3): one correction-type flag. Alongside control failures, this is quite possibly a restatement or revision, which raises the misstatement risk.
Financial pressure (1 of 4): one pressure flag (going concern, covenant problem, revenue/EPS-linked incentive pay, or a capital raise) adds motive, though by itself it is common.
Numeric warning signals (1 of 4 computable): one numeric model or accrual/cash-flow red flag gives some quantitative support but is not strong.
Mitigating: no investigations or litigation (0 of 3), no CEO/CFO turnover (0 of 2), and no transaction-complexity flags (0 of 8), so there is no sign of external scrutiny or aggressive structuring.
Limitation: the card gives only counts by area (no F01-F28 or R01-R19 values), so which specific items are present is unknown and the score is moderated.
